key_insight: EEG-Xplain provides a unified attribution framework to explain black-box EEG foundation models across spatial, temporal, and frequency dimensions.
engineering_relevance: It offers a standardized way to validate interpretability and reliability, helping clinicians and engineers trust EEG models for decision support.
method: Combines gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based attribution methods.
Maps important EEG channels, time segments, and frequency bands with topographic, heatmap, and spectral analyses.
Uses AOPC and cross-method consistency, then converts results into natural-language reports with LLMs.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Mumtaz2016 and TUAB show explanations aligned with known neurophysiological markers while also revealing artifact and spurious-pattern dependencies.
watch_item: Attributions can be unstable across methods or sensitive to artifacts, so explanation quality must be checked carefully before clinical use.
paper_title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models
